attempted_claim: Let P^2={(xi1,xi2,xi1^2+xi2^2):|xii|<=1} in R^3 with R^{-1}-neighbourhood N(R^{-1}). For alpha,beta in [1/2,1], s=alpha+beta, let Gamma_{alpha,beta}(R^{-1}) be the small-cap partition into ~R^{-alpha} x R^{-beta} x R^{-1} caps as in Guth-Maldague-Oh (1.2). Prove for some s>3/2 (toward the conjectured 1<=s<=2) the sharp small-cap decoupling estimate at 2<=p<=2+2/s: ||F||_{L^p(R^3)} <= C_{p,eps} R^{s(1/2-1/p)+eps} (sum_gamma ||P_gamma F||_{L^p}^p)^{1/p} for all F with supp F-hat subset N(R^{-1}), in particular the endpoint p=2+2/s.
decisive_failure: The investigation was bounded to one pass over the admitted toolkit (broad-narrow, bilinear, polynomial partitioning) plus a quantitative deficit model; it does not rule out a future proof using genuinely new Kakeya/incidence input, nor does it establish any impossibility of the conjectured s>3/2 estimate.
